summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and polysubstance use was admitted for acute shortness of breath, leg swelling, and productive cough. He had missed four days of torsemide, leading to fluid overload. He was treated with IV furosemide, transitioned to oral torsemide, and managed for a COPD exacerbation with prednisone and azithromycin. On the day of planned discharge, he experienced a vasovagal episode with transient pulselessness requiring CPR and epinephrine; telemetry showed Afib with RVR, but he achieved ROSC quickly. The event was attributed to over-diuresis and straining, prompting reduction of torsemide to 40mg. Spironolactone was initiated for heart failure. He improved clinically, reached dry weight (216.9 lbs), and was discharged home with follow-up instructions, medication adherence counseling, and daily weight monitoring.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
